data.text/markdown:
TSMixer deep dive: one model per stock

The question stays the one of the day-start notebook: at a fixed time of day, will a stock be up or down at the end of the horizon, and by roughly how much? Stocks behave differently, and one TSMixer for seven stocks at once found nothing (best +0.05, z 1.3), so here every stock gets its own study and its own model, and the stocks are compared afterwards.
  • 40 stocks in six groups: market cap (large, mid, small) × trading volume (high, low), spread over the sectors (Table 1)
  • ten inputs (Table 2), each switchable, chosen from the literature on intraday return predictability and available at least daily
  • one split: TRAIN (the model learns), VALIDATION (every trial is scored), TEST (read once, at the very end)
  • the score: the correlation of the predicted and the actual move to the end of the horizon, checked against luck (random up/down outcomes of the same sizes)
  • run all stocks: one study per stock with a progress bar; each stock's best model is saved; the leaderboard (Table 5) and the groups (Table 6) compare the stocks
  • one stock in detail: its trials, and which inputs its best model leans on

Settings

The next cell holds every setting, in six blocks. Edit a value and everything below re-runs.
  1. The question (fixed): when the prediction is made, and how far ahead it looks
  2. The data: the stocks with their group (each gets its own model) and three consecutive date ranges: TRAIN → VALIDATION → TEST (Table 3 and Figure 0 show the days)
  3. The inputs (Table 2): each one True (read), False (not read) or "search" (the optimizer decides, trial by trial); the stock's own path is always read
  4. What the optimizer searches: the history length and the trials per stock; TSMixer's own knobs are in Table 4
  5. Training (fixed): how many passes, when to stop
  6. Luck check and records: random outcomes per score; W&B on or off

The stocks

Table 1: each stock's group, sector, market cap (today), trading volume and volatility (the three months before TRAIN), and the share of minutes with a trade (the whole window). About a minute the first time, then saved. The low-volume stocks trade in fewer minutes: a stock-day only becomes an example if the stock traded in at least half of the minutes the model reads. Every stock with full 1-minute data since January 2025 has a ticker from C to E (the order of the backfill), so the 40 do too.

data.text/markdown:
One stock: its inputs and its split

Pick a stock (the same pick drives the detail sections at the end; loading it takes about 20 seconds). Table 2 lists the ten inputs: what each one is, why it may carry information (the literature), where it comes from, its setting, and on what share of the stock's days it has a value. Table 3 and Figure 0 show the split:
  • history only: the first 10 sessions, read for the typical sizes, never learned
  • TRAIN: the model learns; its last 10 days are held out to stop the training and to set the size scale β
  • VALIDATION: every trial is scored here; TEST: read once, at the very end
Every input is in the stock's own typical units, measured on earlier sessions only. The market and sector inputs come from a basket of every stock with full 1-minute data (equal weights; the sector basket leaves the stock itself out). Only data available at least daily is used: news, ratings and earnings dates are sporadic, short interest is twice a month.

data.text/markdown:
Run all stocks: one study and one model per stock

run all stocks runs one Optuna study per stock, MAX_TRIALS trials each, one stock after the other; the progress bar shows the stock, the trial, the stock's best so far and the time left. A trial draws the history length, the inputs set to "search", the previous days' length and TSMixer's knobs (Table 4), trains ONE TSMixer on the stock's TRAIN days and scores it on its VALIDATION days.
  • score (maximized): the end-move correlation; the luck check flips each day's move at random; also: hit rate, size error after a scale β from the held-out days, per month
  • resumable: each stock's study is a journal in studies/ (tsmixer-lab-h<horizon>-<batch>-<stock>; the batch is a fingerprint of every setting except the stocks and MAX_TRIALS, and of tsmixer_lab.py). Pressing the button again tops every study up to MAX_TRIALS: an interrupted run continues where it stopped, and a first pass with MAX_TRIALS = 10 (random trials only) can be extended later
  • the models: whenever a trial beats its stock's best so far, its weights are saved to var/tsmixer_lab/models/<batch>/<stock>.ckpt, its settings and scores beside them in <stock>.json (tsmixer_lab.load_model reads them back); every trial's predictions go to var/tsmixer_lab/trials/
  • time: about 20 seconds to load a stock, then 2–4 seconds per trial: 40 stocks × 40 trials is about 1–2 hours. Watch one stock live with uvx optuna-dashboard strategies/darts_forecast/studies/<study>.log

data.text/markdown:
The leaderboard: which stocks have an edge?

Table 5 ranks the stocks by their best trial's luck z. Two warnings:
  • a stock's best is the best of its trials: compare its z with its bar, the z the best of that many trials reaches by luck 2.5% of the time. The first 10 trials are random draws, not chosen by the optimizer: their mean shows the stock without selection
  • picking the best stocks is another selection: the best of 40 stocks, each the best of its trials, has to clear the bar for ALL their trials together (the line above Table 5). Whichever stocks look strongest here must be confirmed on TEST, read once
Table 6 sums up the six groups; Figure 3 draws every stock's best z against its bar.

data.text/markdown:
Which inputs does the stock's best model use?

Measured for the picked stock's best trial only, on its saved model (loaded, not trained again), in two ways: scrambling (Table 8, Figure 7) and SHAP (Table 9, Figures 8 and 9). Both ask what happens when an input is absent, and absent means: read from another day of the same stock, so the input keeps its usual size and only its link to that day's outcome is cut. VALIDATION days only; TEST stays unread. Scrambling (about a minute) scores VALIDATION again with one input scrambled at a time, ten times each, and shows how far the end correlation falls:
  • drop near 0 (inside its sd): the model does not use that input, or it adds nothing
  • drop clearly above its sd, and every scramble hurt: the model leans on it, and it helps on days the model never learned from
  • drop below 0: the model scores better without it: the input hurts out of sample
  • market + sector is also scrambled together: they share most of their information
  • a drop cannot be much bigger than the score the model had: if the stock's best trial is within luck, every drop is small and noisy, and the table says what this one model leans on, not what predicts
Press the button to measure the picked stock's best trial.

data.text/markdown:
SHAP: what each input did to each prediction

The same saved model, now with Shapley values (the shap library, which darts already requires): for one day, how far each input moved the predicted move to the end of the horizon away from what the model predicts with every input absent (an average over ten other days). The values add up exactly: prediction = average with every input absent + the inputs' values. They are signed, so they also say the direction, which scrambling cannot.
  • mean |SHAP|: how much the input moves predictions on average, whether or not that moves them the right way. High here and near 0 in Table 8 means the model moves with the input but it does not help on VALIDATION
  • Figure 8: every explained day; a wide spread is an input that matters on some days
  • Figure 9 (per-day inputs: gap, previous days, same hour): the input's value against its SHAP value; a rising line means a high value pushes the prediction up
  • correlated inputs share the credit (market and sector)
  • about 1.5 seconds per explained day
